mcat_description.short: Prefabricated security cabins are factory-built, portable guard rooms designed to house security personnel at entry/exit points, sold as complete ready-to-install units per piece. They are constructed on mild steel base frames with wall and roof panels made from PUF sandwich panels, GI sheets, FRP, PVC, or cement fibre board.
mcat_description.long: A prefabricated security cabin is a compact, modular structure factory-manufactured to provide a functional and weather-resistant workspace for security guards at access control points. Constructed on a mild steel (MS) base frame, the walls and roof are built using insulated PUF sandwich panels, galvanised iron (GI) sheets, FRP panels, PVC panels, or cement fibre board, with standard sizes ranging from 4'×4' to 8'×8' and custom dimensions available. These cabins typically include sliding or swing doors with locking systems, glazed windows for visibility, pre-fitted electrical conduits, ventilation provisions, and optional air conditioning fitments. They are delivered fully assembled or in semi-knocked-down (SKD) form for rapid on-site deployment at factories, construction sites, gated residential communities, warehouses, offices, and government installations.

market_context: Prefabricated security cabins in India are a well-established segment within the broader portable/modular cabin market, dominated by small-to-mid-size manufacturers supplying pan-India. PUF (Polyurethane Foam) sandwich panel construction is the dominant commercial form, valued for thermal insulation, weather resistance, and lightweight portability — confirmed by EPACK, Niko Prefab, and Hitech Innovations. GI sheet and FRP variants serve cost-sensitive and corrosion-resistant applications respectively, while cement fibre board cabins (as noted in buyer call data) are used where fire resistance or permanence is preferred. Standard cabin sizes range from 4'×4' to 8'×8', with 4'×4'×7' and 6'×4'×7' being the most commonly ordered configurations (Niko Prefab). Relevant Indian standards for PUF panel construction include IS 12436:1988 (polyurethane foam), IS 14246:2013 (PPGI sheet), and IS 277:2018 (zinc coating on GI sheets), with BMTPC Performance Appraisal Certificates (PAC) serving as a quality benchmark for PUF panel systems. Key manufacturers include EPACK Prefab, Pressmach, UNO Structures, Niko Prefab, Zigma Cabin, and Everest Composites. Buyers span industrial, institutional, and government segments; government procurement (CRPF, PWD, defence) often specifies PUF panel huts with MHA/BMTPC-compliant specifications. Cabins are delivered fully assembled or in SKD form, with installation and Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMC) offered by organised manufacturers.
